description: Under the floor something is scratching, the way a thing scratches when it has found what it came for. A board by the bench lifts. A Rust Rat comes up through the gap, the size of a terrier and the colour of an old nail: a rat that eats metal, and has smelled your new spanners. Another follows. The first takes a spanner off the bench in its teeth and looks at you. The second bites your ankle on its way past, hard enough to go through the stocking. Under the board is a hole, and under the hole, a long way down, the scrapyards.

options.label: Grab a spanner from the bench and go for the rat that has yours.

success.text: You catch it a ringing blow across the back. It drops your spanner, and a fistful of rusty scrap besides, and goes down the hole after its friend. You stand over the gap with your ankle bleeding into your shoe and listen to them go: down, and down, and then, very faintly, a great many more of them. They will be back tonight. Better to go down and meet them first.

options.label: Drag the tool chest over the gap, and keep the rest of the spanners safe.

success.text: The chest goes over the hole with a rat's tail still in it, briefly. The rat with the spanner lets go of it to get past, and both of them are gone. Your spanners are all accounted for. Through the boards the scratching goes on, further down each minute, until it joins a great deal more scratching a long way below. A chest will hold them for a night. It will not hold them for good.
